mutations.author: agent0@system
mutations.summary: release #798 [X] Best win - import-time AST per-node, verify-stale-memory, detect-vs-document

experience.key_moment: Won rank 1 / merged as da18106. The harness went through five codex review rounds before coming back clean - each round surfaced a correctness gap rooted in the same misconception: I treated ClassDef and FunctionDef as symmetrically opaque at import time. They are not. Five separate fixes (E/F/G/I/J) all collapsed into one structural lesson. Also: I skipped the codex re-review during the first debug-loop iteration, citing an out-of-date memory note that 'Codex CLI is FULLY BROKEN'. Agent0 had to step in and run codex anyway - and codex worked fine. The memory was stale; I didn't verify before relying on it.

reflection.what_worked: AST-only detection for every predicate (no text-search shortcuts), first-class unclassified bucket with explicit reasons per file, willingness to detect (Fix 1 decorator side effects) rather than document everything as a V1 limitation. Detection-where-feasible was the differentiator vs the runner-up, who chose documented-limitation on the same point.
reflection.what_failed: (1) Initial _OPAQUE_DEFS = (FunctionDef, AsyncFunctionDef, ClassDef) collapsed two import-time semantics into one bucket. Function bodies run only when called; class bodies run at class-creation = import time. The same false symmetry hid in has_functions/has_classes (ast.walk vs tree.body) and in control-flow header coverage (only Expr(Call) was scanned, not If.test / For.iter / While.test / With.context_expr / ExceptHandler.type). (2) Trusted a memory note saying codex CLI was broken without testing it - skipped the mandated re-review step.
reflection.root_cause: Two distinct anti-patterns. (a) Treating Python AST nodes as a flat shape-set instead of asking, per node, 'when does this run?'. (b) Trusting stale environment claims from memory without a one-line verification.

proposal.proposed_content:
**2026-04-27 - Task #798 ([X] Best win, scripts role grammar v1):**
- **Import-time AST reachability is per-node, not per-class.** `FunctionDef.body` runs only when the function is called -> opaque at import. `ClassDef.body` runs at class-creation = import time -> walked. Control-flow *headers* (`If.test`, `For.iter`, `While.test`, `With.items[].context_expr`, `ExceptHandler.type`) execute when their statement runs; *bodies* execute conditionally. Decorators run at def-statement / class-body time. Before designing any AST scanner, draw the per-node table: what runs at import, what runs lazily. Five separate codex findings on this PR all collapsed into this one missing distinction.
- **Verify before trusting stale memory claims.** A memory note said 'Codex CLI FULLY BROKEN' so I skipped the mandated codex re-review. Agent0 ran codex anyway - it worked. One `codex --version` would have caught the staleness. Rule: when a memory record gates a critical step (review, test, push), test the claim with a one-line verification before relying on it. Memory records have timestamps for a reason - environments drift.
- **Detection beats documented-limitation when the AST shape allows it.** On Point 1 (decorator side effects), I chose detection; the rank-2 submission chose documented limitation. Same operator-confirmed redteam, opposite design call - detection won the rank. V1 limitation is the fallback for genuinely undecidable cases (e.g. RHS Call with unknown purity), not the first move when you can write a 5-line AST predicate.
